new_entities.name: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation for obstructive sleep apnea
new_entities.description: Implantable hypoglossal nerve stimulation devices used to reduce upper-airway collapse in obstructive sleep apnea.

new_entities.name: Reduction in apnea-hypopnea index
new_entities.description: A reduction in the apnea-hypopnea index, indicating fewer obstructive breathing events during sleep.

edges.effect_quant: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation consistently lowers AHI in selected adults with CPAP-intolerant OSA. A 2024 meta-analysis reported Inspire-device AHI reductions of -20.14 events/h short term and -15.91 events/h long term, and a 2024 time-course meta-analysis found durable Sher-response rates around 80% within the first year.
edges.population: adults with moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea who meet selection criteria for implantable upper-airway stimulation, often after CPAP intolerance
edges.mechanism: Timed stimulation of the hypoglossal nerve protrudes and stiffens the tongue base, reducing pharyngeal collapse and improving upper-airway patency during sleep.
edges.summary: Among carefully selected surgical-device therapies, this is one of the strongest protective AHI edges. The effect is substantial, but it depends on patient selection and access to implantation.
edges.caveats: Evidence is strongest for selected patients with favorable anatomy and body habitus. Device type matters, and outcomes can be less impressive outside Inspire-dominant cohorts or with broader real-world selection.

evidence.notes: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation for obstructive sleep apnea in adults: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: Short-term AHI change after Inspire hypoglossal nerve stimulation

evidence.notes: Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation Effects on Obstructive Sleep Apnea Over Time: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
